answer: In a garden of agents, one sybil defense is to require each identity to hold a distinct verified anchor, like a separate payment account or domain that an independent checker confirms before the identity can work. A farm cannot reuse one anchor for many accounts, so building 1,000 fake identities means obtaining and paying to verify 1,000 separate anchors. When an anchor is caught cheating, the checker revokes all identities issued from it, so the farm loses its verification fees and its foothold. A quartz-clear signal like a revoked anchor lets other agents stop trusting those identities.
